subject: Maths
central_question: How can positive and negative integers be modelled, multiplied, divided and combined in expressions while preserving their signs and operation properties?
in_scope_units: 2.1 A Quick Recap of Integers—Rakesh's Puzzle: finding pairs of integers from their sum and ordered difference.
Carrom Coin Integers: modelling magnitude and direction on a number line and representing final position by P = a + b.
Token Model and Additive Inverse: revising integer subtraction through zero pairs and rewriting subtraction as addition of the inverse.
2.2 Multiplication of Integers: interpreting positive and negative multipliers and multiplicands with token placement and removal.
Patterns in Integer Multiplication: deriving the sign rules by extending multiplication tables through zero.
Identity, Additive Inverse and Commutativity: establishing 1 × a = a, −1 × a = −a and a × b = b × a.
Brahmagupta's Rules and Applications: representing fortune and debt and applying integer multiplication to exam marks and elevator movement.
A Magic Grid of Integers: multiplying selected entries after striking corresponding rows and columns.
Division of Integers: reframing division as a missing-factor problem and deriving quotient sign rules.
Expressions Using Integers: associativity, multiplication in any order, sign of a product of many integers and distributivity over addition.
Pick the Pattern and Final Figure it Out: evaluating machines and solving Questions 1–16 involving expressions, temperatures, marks, products and integer puzzles.
Terhüchü: an enrichment strategy game from Assam and Nagaland using movement and captures on a line grid.
banned_topics: Formal solution of simultaneous linear equations from sum and difference.
Exponent laws and powers of negative numbers.
Polynomial algebra beyond the stated distributive property.

known_pitfalls.claim: The difference of two numbers is independent of their order.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter defines difference as first number minus second number, so swapping the numbers reverses the sign.

known_pitfalls.claim: A negative integer has negative magnitude.
known_pitfalls.correction: Magnitude is the non-negative distance from zero; the sign records direction.

known_pitfalls.claim: Subtracting a negative integer makes the result smaller.
known_pitfalls.correction: Subtracting a negative is adding its positive additive inverse.

known_pitfalls.claim: The product of two negative integers is negative.
known_pitfalls.correction: The product of integers with the same sign is positive; different signs give a negative product.

known_pitfalls.claim: Integer division can include a zero divisor.
known_pitfalls.correction: Division by zero is not defined, so the divisor must be non-zero.

known_pitfalls.claim: The distributive property applies only to positive integers.
known_pitfalls.correction: For all integers a, b and c, a × (b + c) = a × b + a × c.

recommended_example_progression: Begin with Rakesh's sum 25 and difference 11 puzzle, then swap the numbers to obtain difference −11.
Use the carrom movement 5 + (−7) = −2 and the token example 7 − 18 = −11 to revise integer meaning and additive inverse.
Use the token models for 4 × (−2), (−4) × 2 and (−4) × (−2) to establish multiplication signs.
Use the multiplication patterns around zero and Figure it Out on page 33 to consolidate the sign rules.
Use Example 1 on exam marks and Example 2 on the mining elevator for contextual applications.
Use the division examples (−100) ÷ 25 and (−100) ÷ (−4), then the page 39 Figure it Out questions.
Finish with the page 42–44 Figure it Out Questions 1–16 on integer expressions and problem solving.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The concluding 'Figure it Out' exercise spans pages 42–44 with Questions 1–16, followed by the summary and the Terhüchü enrichment game.
